CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up regarding recent hospitalization for infection concerns.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Michelle King is a 43-year-old female with a history of quadriplegia from a prior spinal cord injury. She was recently hospitalized at District Regional Hospital from 06/29/2021 to 07/02/2021 for evaluation of spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and diaphoresis. In the emergency department, she was found to be febrile with a significantly elevated white blood cell count of 23,000. She presented with labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. She was treated with intravenous antibiotic therapy with clinical improvement and was discharged after a few days. The patient reports that she believes her hospitalization was primarily related to constipation rather than a urinary tract infection. She notes that upon arriving home, she had a significant bowel movement and felt markedly better. She states that she had not had a regular bowel movement in some time prior to admission despite taking miralax daily. Urine cultures obtained during hospitalization were not impressive. Review of recent records shows that her white count has sometimes been mildly elevated, though it was normal last year. The patient was admitted during an extremely hot period in late June. She is currently back to her baseline and denies current pain or discomfort.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports feeling back to her normal self. She denies pain or discomfort anywhere. She has a regular bowel regimen with daily miralax and uses lactulose as a rescue medication for severe constipation, though she notes it takes about two days to work and the effects are severe. She stays indoors more during hot weather to manage heat exposure.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Quadriplegia from prior spinal cord injury
Chronic constipation
Recent hospitalization for infection evaluation (June 2021)
Suprapubic catheter

MEDICATIONS
Miralax daily for constipation management
Lactulose as rescue medication for constipation
Vitamin C supplement
Multivitamins

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is unvaccinated against COVID-19. She expresses hesitation regarding vaccination due to concerns about unknown side effects and reports of "vaccine injury." She believes she is young and healthy enough to fight COVID-19 despite having limited respiratory function. She takes vitamin C and multivitamins as supplements. She does not receive annual flu vaccinations. She is described as somewhat homeopathic in her health philosophy.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally
General: Patient appears well
Cardiovascular: No abnormalities noted
Abdomen: Not specifically examined
Neurological: No acute concerns noted
Pain: Denies pain or discomfort anywhere

RESULTS
Recent hospitalization labs showed elevated WBC of 23,000. Urine cultures obtained during hospitalization were not impressive for significant infection. X-rays were performed during admission. Historical WBC was normal last year.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute to chronic constipation: Patient's recent hospitalization appears more likely related to severe constipation and possible autonomic dysreflexia from her quadriplegia rather than a true urinary tract infection. Dehydration during the extremely hot period in late June may have exacerbated her constipation. Current bowel regimen includes miralax daily as primary treatment with lactulose available as a rescue medication. Plan to return in 2-3 weeks for fasting laboratory studies including a complete blood count to ensure her elevated white blood cell count normalizes. If WBC remains elevated, further investigation for bowel pathology will be warranted. Patient will also obtain cholesterol panel as she is due for lipid screening.

2. Quadriplegia: Status post spinal cord injury with resulting quadriplegia. Recent vital sign changes and symptoms likely related to autonomic dysreflexia. Continue current management and monitoring.

3. COVID-19 vaccine status: Patient is currently unvaccinated and hesitant. Discussed vaccine safety and emphasized that she is at high risk given her quadriplegia status. Explained that the vaccine is the only true preventative mechanism for COVID-19 and that supplements will not provide adequate protection. Advised against relying on treatments such as monoclonal antibodies as alternatives. Doctor strongly recommends vaccination given patient's high-risk status, noting that untreated COVID-19 could be particularly dangerous for her. Patient is asked to consider the recommendation and may follow up with additional questions.
